Sure! If you only need the **IDs** and **context attributes** (i.e., the minimal set of fields) for the CAA records of `sample2.com`, you can use the API’s “list” endpoint with a *fields* filter. Here’s a quick step‑by‑step guide: | Step | What to do | Example | |------|------------|---------| | 1 | **Set up your API key** – put it in the `Authorization` header or as a query parameter, depending on your provider’s convention. | `Authorization: Bearer secret567` | | 2 | **Choose the endpoint** – most DNS providers expose something like `/domains/{domain}/records`. For CAA records, you’ll usually add a type filter (`type=CAA`). | `GET https://api.dnsprovider.com/v1/domains/sample2.com/records?type=CAA` | | 3 | **Add a fields filter** – specify only the fields you want. Common names are `id` and `context`. | `&fields=id,context` | | 4 | **Send the request** – you can use `curl`, Postman, or any HTTP client. | `curl -H "Authorization: Bearer secret567" "https://api.dnsprovider.com/v1/domains/sample2.com/records?type=CAA&fields=id,context"` | | 5 | **Parse the response** – you’ll receive a JSON array where each object contains just `id` and `context`. | ```json
{
"records": [
{ "id": "12345", "context": { ... } },
{ "id": "67890", "context": { ... } }
]
}
``` | ### Quick Reference ```bash curl -H "Authorization: Bearer secret567" \ "https://api.dnsprovider.com/v1/domains/sample2.com/records?type=CAA&fields=id,context" ``` - **`type=CAA`** – filters to only CAA records. - **`fields=id,context`** – tells the API to return only those two fields. If your provider uses a different query syntax (e.g., `?filter[type]=CAA` or `?select=id,context`), just swap out the parameters accordingly. That’s all you need to pull just the IDs and context attributes for `sample2.com`’s CAA records. Let me know if you run into any hiccups!
